Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

atlantio 0.6.0

  • New write_run_script() and run_atlantis() to run a model. write_run_script() renders the Atlantis command line of a run directory from the template inst/run_scripts/script.sh (with the path to the binary if it is not on the PATH) and creates its output folder. run_atlantis() runs it, directly or in a Docker container (as the current user, with other folders mounted read-only), with a time limit (a container that reaches it is removed, as killing the Docker client leaves it running), and checks with check_run() that it completed: Atlantis exits with status 0 after a fatal error. Its result adds check and complete to that of processx::run(). The calibration article uses them instead of its own copies.
  • New plot_foodweb() draws the food web of a model with ggplot2: groups placed by trophic level and habitat (pelagic, benthic), edges from prey to predator with a width given by pPREY, and, when the biomass index is loaded, node size and colour given by the initial biomass and the final / initial ratio. highlight takes a table of links (prey, predator, colour, optionally pathway) to highlight; links absent from the food web are drawn dashed. focus restricts the plot to some groups, the groups they interact with and the links involving them.
  • check_prm() and check_run() read a parameter file without keys (empty, or comments only). They failed with “arguments imply differing number of rows”; check_run() now says that tstop is not found.

atlantio 0.5.0

  • The run_model() of the calibration article records a run whose scoring fails as failed. It saved it as completed, with the penalty score, so summarise_calibration() counted it among the completed runs. It also closes the output it reads.
  • The example outputs that nothing used (outputPROD.nc, outputTOT.nc, export.ts, inputs.ts, tiny_groups.xml and tiny_run.xml) are removed: the package is 2 MB smaller.
  • Fewer messages. read_atlantis_files() no longer prints the column specification of every text output, nor an alert for a file it cannot read, which atlantis_load_files() reports: a missing file gives one warning (it gave three). create_time_series() and create_time_series_biomass() say that layer or age is ignored only when it was given. Printing an Atlantis object whose geometry has no depth no longer warns.
  • An atlantis_check table subset by columns prints as a data frame. It printed “0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.” above the rows.
  • atlantis_load_files() aborts when files is neither file paths nor an atlantis_file object. It printed an alert and returned the object unchanged.
  • check_prm() and check_run() read the time units of the run file as Atlantis does. Atlantis converts a time with its unit only if the unit is spelled exactly as one of its units (s, min, hour, day, week, …); otherwise it ignores the unit and reads the value in seconds, e.g. for tstop 100 days, tstop 100 Day, tstop 2 year, or a unit that ends a line with Windows (CRLF) line endings. check_prm() reports these units as errors (it noted them as converted), and check_run() checks the run against the seconds Atlantis reads (it converted these units). The "units" check now covers only the times of the run file, the only values Atlantis converts.
  • check_prm() reports a key given twice in the run file as an error: Atlantis reads its first occurrence, while read_prm() keeps the last. In the other files, the warning says that Atlantis may read another occurrence. check_run() reads the first occurrence of tstop and toutinc, as Atlantis does; it read the last.
  • create_diet_table() names the sediment detritus columns after the detritus groups of the groups file. It assumed DL, DR and DC.
  • create_foodweb() works with a single predator (it failed with “incorrect number of dimensions”) and with group codes holding a digit (it cut them at the digit), and checks the groups file before the diet table.
  • create_time_series_biomass() aborts when boundary = FALSE leaves no box, and create_time_series() when box is empty. Both failed with “arguments imply differing number of rows”.
  • generate_calibration_table() gives no row, with a warning, for an entry whose values are all in ignored_values; it failed with “arguments imply differing number of rows”. Its error for a missing value shows why the value is needed (the hint was lost).
  • generate_calibration_table() reads the parameters of version, once. It ignored version and read the parameter list for every entry.
  • generate_file() writes the time step as dt 12 hour. It wrote dt 12 Hours, which Atlantis reads as 12 seconds.
  • generate_file() needs file: it wrote run.prm into the working directory by default. It writes an array given in ... (init_scalar) as its length, with the values on the next line, as Atlantis reads it; it wrote R code (init_scalar c(1, 2, 3)). It writes the placeholder <<TO_EDIT>> as documented (not <<TO_EDIT>>>), and warns about names in ... that are not run parameters, which it ignores.
  • generate_file() and write_prm() write LF line endings on every platform. On Windows they wrote CRLF, and Atlantis reads the carriage return as part of a unit that ends a line: tstop 365 day was 365 seconds.
  • get_biomass_by_type() returns the annual biomass at age ("biomass_age_annual"), as the Get Started article says, and aborts on an unknown type. It returned NULL for both, after an alert.
  • input_files matches the Atlantis class: the detailed diet output is named diet_detailed, as the property (it was detail_diet, so atlantis_load_files() never recorded its path), the age biomass outputs have the names Atlantis writes (AgeBiomIndx.txt, AnnualAgeBiomIndx.txt), and the physics and forcing files have a row.
  • read_calibration_runs() names a run after its folder relative to dir, so runs in nested folders with the same name stay apart, matches the file name exactly, and no longer reads par_model as par when par is missing. summarise_calibration() gathers the runs without generation in the generation NA; generations and scores were NULL when no run had one.
  • read_nc() closes a netCDF file it does not recognise, and check_run() an output without time dimension; both stayed open.
  • read_prm() also keeps the units us, usec, ms and msec after a value. It read them as comments, so write_prm() wrote the value without its unit.
  • read_prm() reads an empty file as an empty list, and no longer warns about a missing final newline.
  • score_table() and compute_score() abort when a series has no value at t = 0, with the groups concerned. They failed with “..1 must be of size …” or “subscript out of bounds”.
  • set_init_values() removes the copy it made when it fails.
  • transform_parameter_value() computes pow10 and pow2 exactly (10^2 is 100; it gave 100.00000000000004).
  • write_parameter_folder() aborts rather than change a key given several times in its file, as Atlantis may read another occurrence than the one changed. It changed the last one.

atlantio 0.4.0

  • atlantis_load_files() says why a file cannot be read. It said that the file did not exist, and reported only the first of several such files. Loading a run file no longer warns about the keys missing from the run template, which check_prm() reports.
  • check_run() checks that a run completed: Atlantis exits with status 0 after a fatal error, so a run counts as complete only if the last time step of its main output reaches tstop (within one toutinc), read with its units as Atlantis reads them.
  • create_diet_table(), create_foodweb(), create_time_series(), create_time_series_biomass() and generate_calibration_table() are functions rather than S7 generics, so their help pages document their arguments. They no longer accept unused arguments.
  • The help of create_diet_table() swapped predator and prey: its rows are the predators (with the stages) and its columns the prey, and the edges of create_foodweb() go from predator to prey.
  • create_time_series_biomass() converts the nitrogen of biomass pools to wet weight with X_CN and k_wetdry, as for the age-structured groups. It used 1 + X_RS, which made pool weights about 30 times too low.
  • create_time_series_biomass() returns the epibenthic groups (one value per box, in mg N m-2), weighted by the box area of the geometry file. It returned no row for them.
  • create_time_series_biomass() gains boundary: boundary = FALSE leaves out the boundary boxes, as Atlantis’ biomass index does.
  • create_time_series_biomass() labels biomass pools with the group name (it used the variable name, e.g. Diatom_N) and an NA age, and labels correctly the groups whose name holds a digit.
  • Writing a parameter set back into a parameter folder:
    • apply_parameters() sets the values of a calibration table (on the calibration or the model scale) in the parameter files loaded in an Atlantis object;
    • write_parameter_folder() writes the input files of an Atlantis object into a folder, optionally on top of a copy of another folder (for the files not loaded, such as the physics and forcing files). The run and biology files are patched in place, only the values that changed, so their comments, units, layout and line endings are kept;
    • compare_prm() compares two parameter files by parameter name.
  • Summarising a calibration: read_calibration_runs() collects the parameters.rds of every run, and summarise_calibration() gives, per parameter value, the best run, the range of the best runs and the median of the top runs (as factors of the starting value or as values), how many top runs sit at a bound, how failed runs differ from completed ones, and the values and scores per generation.
  • The atlantis_check tables of check_init(), check_prm() and check_run() now print as a summary when the package is installed (the print method was registered on a copy of print() left in the namespace by the S7 print method of Atlantis).
  • The vignettes cover the new functions: checking the inputs and the runs in Get Started, and in the calibration vignette, check_run() and apply_parameters() / write_parameter_folder() in the objective function, and a new step 5 summarising the runs and writing the next parameter folder.
  • new_atlantis() matches property names exactly: new_atlantis(diet_detailed = d) also set diet.
  • read_atlantis_files() uses filenames when given several files. It ignored them, so renamed outputs (e.g. Shiny uploads) were not recognised.
  • read_prm() keeps the time unit after a value (e.g. day in tstop 365 day) as the attribute unit, and write_prm() writes it back. write_prm() wrote the number alone, which Atlantis reads in seconds.
  • read_prm() reads arrays whose first value has a sign (e.g. -1 2 3). Such rows were skipped, so the array was read as its count.
  • score_table() and compute_score() gain method = "lnorm2", the objective function of Morell et al. (2026) as in their calibration code (squared log ratio to the target summed over the scored values, no band, on the weight-at-age and the biomass by default), and weight and target_factor (Morell et al.’s b) per tracer, for both methods.

atlantio 0.3.0

  • New calibration objective functions:
    • score_table() and compute_score() score how far a run drifts from its initial state (log ratio to t = 0, a no-penalty band per tracer, squared excess beyond the band), per group x age x tracer or in total, on the age-structured tracers and optionally on the biomass of every living group;
    • window_values() reduces a series to its scored values over the last years of a run (yearly snapshots or a statistic such as the mean);
    • aggregate_time_series() aggregates the tracer table of create_time_series_biomass() over boxes and layers (Nums summed, StructN and ResN weighted by Nums);
    • read_biomass_index() reads the biomass index of the living groups.
  • create_time_series_biomass() gains aggregate: with aggregate = TRUE the series are reduced over boxes and layers while they are read, one cohort at a time, so the per-box table of a whole run is never held in memory (peak memory of a Lake Erie run roughly halved).
  • aggregate_time_series() sums a weight column and keeps units.
  • New checks of the model input files, both returning an atlantis_check table (one row per finding: file, check, severity, key, message):
    • check_init() checks an initial-conditions file in the cells Atlantis uses: NaN, negative values, cells left unset where Atlantis silently uses a non-zero _FillValue, groups switched on but empty or missing, and pools far from the other groups of their type;
    • check_prm() scans parameter files line by line (so a malformed array does not stop it): array counts that do not match their values, duplicated keys, CRLF line endings, tabs, units after values, unknown run keys, and the stocking traps (flagstocking with flagrecruit 18, flagrandom 1 with stocking, stocking never on the spawn day).
  • set_init_values() sets a variable of an initial-conditions file per box and layer from a table.

atlantio 0.2.2

  • generate_calibration_table() can calibrate the linear and quadratic mortality rates <GRP>_mL and <GRP>_mQ, now listed in the parameter dictionary with the new dimension per_stage: one value per stage, read from the NumStages column of the groups file (2 for juvenile/adult groups, 1 otherwise).
  • The Beverton-Holt recruitment parameters BHalpha_<GRP> and BHbeta_<GRP> are listed in the parameter dictionary, so they can be calibrated.
  • generate_calibration_table() expands placeholder keys of non-array type (e.g. mum_<GRP>_T15, C_<GRP>_T15) to a single value per key; they were given one position per group, all but the first with no current value.

atlantio 0.2.1

  • generate_calibration_table():
    • expands names with several placeholders (only the last one was replaced), e.g. pPREY<PREYCOHORT><PRED><PREDCOHORT>;
    • gains the field ignored_values to leave out positions holding given values, e.g. ignored_values: 0 to calibrate only existing diet links;
    • checks positions of per_prey parameters (one value per group plus one per detritus group);
    • caps the bounds of proportion parameters (e.g. pPREY) to [0, 1].
  • The diet availability key is now listed as pPREY<PREYCOHORT><PRED><PREDCOHORT>: the first digit is the prey stage, the last one the predator stage (the two were swapped).

atlantio 0.2.0

  • generate_calibration_table() supports is_factor, when true, min and maxare interpreted relative to the current value of the parameter rather than as absolute bounds.
  • atlantis_load_files() no longer drops files when several files of the same type are passed, and skips files of unsupported type (e.g. unknown, xml_file) with a warning instead of erroring.
  • read_txt_files() classifies DietCheck outputs as diet and DetailedDietCheck outputs as diet_detailed, and always returns a type.
  • create_time_series_biomass() now detects all cohorts of groups with 10 or more age classes (the cohort index was truncated to its last digit).
  • generate_calibration_table() no longer errors on per_box parameters.
  • require_valid_group() reports only the groups that are missing or turned off, instead of all groups passed.
  • Move sf to Suggests.
  • Add calibrar script.

atlantio 0.1.0

  • Initial version. The input/output functionalities of the calypso package have been extracted into this package; the Shiny application now lives in calypso, which builds on top of atlantio.
  • Includes:
    • list_atlantis_parameters() that returns the list of Atlantis parameters for a supported Atlantis version (see the new dataset atlantis_supported_versions);
    • the S7 class Atlantis that represents an Atlantis model, with the constructor new_atlantis() and the loader atlantis_load_files();
    • reading functions for Atlantis files: read_atlantis_files(), read_bgm(), read_nc(), read_prm(), read_prm_files(), read_group_file(), read_txt_files(), read_xml();
    • a prm writer: write_prm();
    • parameter file generation with generate_file() (run file only);
    • S7 methods for Atlantis objects: print(), create_diet_table(), create_foodweb(), create_time_series(), create_time_series_biomass(), generate_calibration_table().
